problem: The vector-valued function $r(y,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x={sin}^{2}⁡y$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [0,\pi ].$ Which of the following could be $r?$

feedback.problem:
$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨\text{__________},\,({2}^{z}-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(z,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y={2}^{z}-1$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis for $z\in [0,2].$ What is the first component of $r?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/04de4ea7dc617be1429c596812ce4f450c2cdaafd8d94d86f75e68a6743acba9.png)

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(z)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis has the position vector 

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(z)={2}^{z}-1\ge 0$ for all $z\in [0,2].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨({2}^{z}-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,({2}^{z}-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [0,2],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Therefore, the first component of $r$ is $({2}^{z}-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
